companyIntro.name: Greenfield Sustainability
companyIntro.mission: Measure and reduce environmental impact with credible, auditable data.
companyIntro.culture: No claim without evidence. Boundaries, factors and sources are always stated.

projectBackground.name: Corporate Carbon Footprint — Halden Foods
projectBackground.timeline: Report due before the annual meeting
projectBackground.context: Halden wants to claim 'carbon-neutral packaging'. You must establish the footprint and test the claim.

manager.name: Maja Lindqvist
manager.role: Head of ESG Advisory, Greenfield Sustainability
manager.note: If it can't be traced to data, it can't be claimed. Boundaries, factors and sources, every time.

assignment.title: Measure the footprint and test the claim
assignment.brief: Classify scopes, calculate Scope 1 and 2 emissions and intensity, complete a site table in Excel and review the claim.

documents.name: Energy Data
documents.note: Electricity 500,000 kWh at 0.4 kg CO2e per kWh; natural gas 80,000 m³ at 2.0 kg CO2e per m³.

documents.name: Marketing Draft
documents.note: 'Our packaging is carbon-neutral' — no offset evidence supplied.

tasks.title: Scope 2 Emissions
tasks.prompt: Electricity 500,000 kWh x 0.4 kg CO2e/kWh. What are the emissions in tonnes CO2e?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Scope 1 + 2 Total
tasks.prompt: Natural gas 80,000 m³ x 2.0 kg = 160 t (Scope 1). Add Scope 2 of 200 t. What is the total (tCO2e)?
tasks.reasoning: Totals combine scopes without double counting.
tasks.mistake: Adding Scope 3 estimates to the same table without labelling mixes quality.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Emissions Intensity
tasks.prompt: 360 tCO2e on €12 million revenue. What is intensity (tCO2e per € million)?
tasks.tip: Pick a denominator that fits the business.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Classification
tasks.prompt: Company vehicles burning diesel are which scope?
tasks.tip: Scope 2: purchased energy. Scope 3: value chain.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Site Emissions (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Emissions in tCO2e (D = B x C / 1000) for each site. Upload for checking.
tasks.mistake: Applying one average factor distorts hot spots.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Claim Review
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence review of the 'carbon-neutral packaging' claim.
tasks.modelAnswer: We cannot support the claim as written. Halden's Scope 1 and 2 footprint is 360 tCO2e and no verified offsets or reductions have been provided; Scope 3 emissions from packaging materials are unmeasured. I recommend replacing it with a factual statement, such as the intensity of 30 tCO2e per € million and the reduction plan. If neutrality is pursued, offsets must be verified, retired and disclosed with the boundary.
tasks.reasoning: A good claim review states what's evidenced, what's not and a compliant alternative.
tasks.mistake: Approving unsupported claims creates legal and reputational risk.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Green Label
caseStudy.background: A company labelled products 'climate positive' on the basis of an internal estimate. A regulator found no evidence and ordered withdrawal of the campaign and a fine.
caseStudy.challenges: No verified data behind the claim.
caseStudy.solution: Greenfield introduced a claims checklist: boundary, method, verification and review before publication.
